newsitem.title: INDIA: India firm confirms Nomura seeking stake.
newsitem.headline: India firm confirms Nomura seeking stake.

text.p: India's UTI Securities confirmed on Friday that Japan's Nomura Securities Co Ltd was interested in buying a 40 percent equity stake in the state-run mutual fund firm.
"They have shown interest in buying a 40 percent stake in UTI Securities," M.K. Khanna, managing director of UTI Securities, told Reuters by telephone from Bombay.
"The formal agreements are yet to be signed," Khanna said.
UTI Securities is a stockbroking and investment company set up in November 1994 by the Unit Trust of India, the country's largest state-run mutual fund.

"UTI Securities was promoted by Unit Trust of India with a paid-up capital of 300 million rupees ($8.4 million)," Khanna said. "The proposal will provide intermediary services to Nomura's international clients."
"We will get added capacity to our debt and equity accounts outside India".
UTI Securities has accounts of about 90 foreign financial institutions, Khanna said.
"In the last two years we had a combined debt and equity turnover of about 73 billion rupees ($2.04 billion)," he said. ($1=35.80 rupees)
